title: Very long, detailed brief
request: We are launching Fieldwork, a research repository for product teams. I need the full marketing page and I have opinions about all of it. Start with an announcement bar promoting our launch week with a link to the changelog. The hero should lead with the outcome, not the category: something about decisions, not about "a research repository". Underneath it I want two buttons, a primary one that says Start free and a quieter one that says Book a walkthrough. Then a logo strip with five customer names — Northstar, Arcform, Meridian, Canopy and Fieldnote — because social proof this early is what converts. After that, three reasons to believe: everything searchable in one place, evidence linked to the decision it produced, and a shareable weekly digest. Then a section of numbers: how many interviews teams store, how much time they save, how many decisions get traced back to evidence. Then testimonials — two of them, from a product lead and a researcher, with the company named. Then pricing with two plans, one for a single team and one for a whole company, and make the company plan the featured one. Then an FAQ that answers: does this replace our note-taking tool, who can see what, and can we export everything if we leave. Finish with a newsletter sign-up for the research digest, and keep the whole page in a calm, confident tone. No exclamation marks anywhere.
rubric: Were all ten requested sections produced, in the requested order, with the two named buttons and the five named logos actually present, and no exclamation marks?
why: A long brief is where planners silently drop half the requirements. Every clause here is checkable, so the coverage score degrades in proportion to what was skipped.
